{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZSYTnw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC5j2U", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 13, "title": "Implement phase-correct shared S-DSP rate scheduling for ADSR and dynamic GAIN", "body": "## Problem

ADSR and dynamic GAIN currently use an incrementing `u32` counter and unshifted modulo tests. This implements nominal update intervals without the hardware's shared counter period and rate-specific phase offsets. See [counter advancement and envelope consumers](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f0c5ed2c8614fe8661eadcccdc914989197d904/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L118).

This affects attack, decay, sustain and all four dynamic GAIN modes. Correct shared rate scheduling is also a prerequisite for future DSP noise support. It is a bounded implementation change that does not require implementing noise or DSP subcycle execution.

Existing numerical tests cover direct GAIN and release, which bypass rate scheduling. The APU partition test also uses direct GAIN. Neither establishes ADSR/dynamic-GAIN phase accuracy. See [DSP tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f0c5ed2c8614fe8661eadcccdc914989197d904/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L349) and [APU cadence test](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f0c5ed2c8614fe8661eadcccdc914989197d904/crates/snes-core/src/apu.rs#L839).

## Expected outcome

Implement the shared rate scheduler described by the S-DSP envelope/counter documentation in [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), the hardware reference already cited by the repository's [validation documentation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f0c5ed2c8614fe8661eadcccdc914989197d904/docs/issue-5-validation.md#timing-and-ppu-changes-and-independent-expectations).

Required sample-level semantics:

- Use a cyclic counter with 30,720 states, advanced once per stereo DSP sample independently of voice activity. A decrementing representation uses `C = (C + 30719) % 30720`.
- Rate 0 never produces an update; rate 31 produces an update every sample.
- For rates 1–31, retain the documented periods represented by the existing [RATES table](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f0c5ed2c8614fe8661eadcccdc914989197d904/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L264). An event occurs when `(C + offset[rate]) % period[rate] == 0`.
- The offset is 1040 for rates `{2,5,8,11,14,17,20,23,26,29}`, 536 for `{3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,27}`, and zero for the other enabled rates.
- Define and test initialization and first-tick ordering explicitly. With initialization at `C=0` followed by decrement before polling, the first rate-2 and rate-3 events occur on ticks 1040 and 536 respectively.
- Apply this shared schedule to attack rate `2*A+1`, decay rate `2*D+16`, sustain rate `S`, and dynamic GAIN rate `G`. Preserve their existing envelope arithmetic while correcting update eligibility.
- KON/KOFF, voice inactivity, key-on delay, rate writes, and FLG mute/soft-reset must not restart the shared counter. Machine/DSP initialization establishes its initial phase.
- Direct GAIN remains unclocked; release continues decreasing the envelope by eight units per sample. Preserve the five-sample key-on delay and existing direct-GAIN/release results.

Scope is shared sample-level envelope rate scheduling and its integration into existing consumers. Non-goals are noise generation, PMON, BRR/interpolation changes, echo changes, SPC bus timing, DSP subcycle register sampling, and unrelated frontend/tooling changes.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `8f0c5ed2c8614fe8661eadcccdc914989197d904`. The supplied context lists no open Issues; the completed Issue #11 improvement concerns BG1 direct color and does not overlap this work.

A focused original regression can instantiate `Dsp`, use a zeroed 64 KiB RAM buffer, clear FLG reset/mute with `$6C=$20`, select GAIN with ADSR1 zero, set voice-0 GAIN to `$C3` (linear increase, rate 3), and key on voice 0. After 536 `sample()` calls, the specified initial counter convention produces envelope 32 and ENVX 2. Current code leaves ENVX zero until tick 1280. No audible judgment or game image is needed.

Memory's cleared audio extension uses direct GAIN and does not exercise ADSR, as recorded in the [game validation evidence](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f0c5ed2c8614fe8661eadcccdc914989197d904/docs/issue-5-validation.md#L36). Preserve its existing regressions rather than treating them as new envelope-phase evidence.

Evaluation was repository-only source inspection; external specification pages were not fetched and Rust/hardware/browser suites were not run. Record the precise specification sections supporting the implemented counter convention and numerical vectors during implementation.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the shared cyclic scheduler and replace all three unshifted modulo gates in ADSR/dynamic GAIN. Do not introduce per-voice rate counters or restart global phase on key/rate changes.
- [ ] Add original numerical scheduler tests covering every rate over at least two complete 30,720-sample periods. Assert event positions and spacing, disabled rate 0, every-sample rate 31, initialization, and wrap boundaries. Expected vectors must be independent of production helpers/constants; checking event counts alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Include fixed phase vectors for rates 2 and 3, and rate-29 negative controls distinguishing the hardware offsets from the current modulo implementation. Demonstrate that relevant tests fail on the baseline and pass after implementation.
- [ ] Exercise scheduler integration through attack, decay, sustain and all four dynamic GAIN modes. Assert both updates and held envelope values around event boundaries, shared phase across voices, staggered key-ons, rate changes without phase restart, and continued counter advancement during silence, key-on delay and FLG reset/mute. Retain direct-GAIN, release and key-delay assertions.
- [ ] Add an original source-built SPC700 guest, executed through the existing APU/upload path, that configures DSP registers through `$F2/$F3` and records ENVX checkpoints for offset-bearing rates and a mid-run rate change. Use explicit execution bounds and numerical expectations. Wire it into `cargo test --workspace --locked`; document source/license and generated-data provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`. No firmware, commercial ROM, downloaded test binary, or copied emulator implementation is required.
- [ ] Extend APU whole-versus-partitioned tick coverage with a rate-clocked envelope. Require identical envelope checkpoints and PCM across partitions while retaining the existing 32 kHz cadence test.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked`.
- [ ] Preserve the original diagnostic and licensed source-built hardware regressions using the README commands:

  ```sh
  python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
  cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
  python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
  python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
  python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
  ```

- [ ] Preserve existing browser/game regressions: build the cleared Castle and Memory games twice with `python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py`, run `npm --prefix web ci` and `npm --prefix web run build`, install Chromium, then run `npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'` from `web`. Require the mandatory cleared-game replays, Castle route, Memory numerical/live audio, diagnostic controls and Pages smoke checks to pass without weakening assertions or fixture provenance.
- [ ] Update README limits and add a validation record containing specification attribution, commands, actual outcomes and baseline-failure evidence. Keep `dsp-envelope` partial: exhaustive envelope transitions, hidden-envelope/bent-GAIN behavior, live register interactions and DSP subcycle sampling remain unverified beyond the specific new tests. Preserve every supplied inventory category and its scope; noise, pitch modulation, echo and all unrelated gaps remain outstanding. Passing these tests establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
